recognize_zh: Perls 鐵染色高倍下，中央巨噬細胞的樹枝狀胞質內有粗大、深藍黑色的含鐵血黃素顆粒，而周圍被紅色複染的紅血球前驅細胞胞質內幾乎看不到藍色鐵顆粒，表示鐵囤積在巨噬細胞、未被紅血球系利用。
features: Central macrophage with dendritic cytoplasmic processes containing coarse blue-black hemosiderin globules
Iron granules of variable size, from fine dots to large round aggregates
Surrounding erythroid precursors (red nuclear counterstain) largely lacking visible cytoplasmic siderotic granules
No ring sideroblasts identified in this field
Orange-staining background red cells and plasma
describe_en: Perls (Prussian blue) stain of a bone marrow aspirate at high power shows a macrophage with dendritic processes containing abundant coarse blue-black hemosiderin granules and globules. The adjacent erythroid precursors, highlighted by the red counterstain, show few or no cytoplasmic siderotic granules, and no ring sideroblasts are seen in this field. This pattern of increased macrophage storage iron with reduced sideroblastic iron indicates impaired iron utilization (reticuloendothelial iron block), as seen in anemia of chronic disease/inflammation; clinical correlation is required.

ddx.vs: Also has increased storage iron, but erythroid precursors show coarse perinuclear siderotic granules encircling at least one-third of the nucleus.
Shows absent storage iron in marrow macrophages and absent sideroblasts, the opposite of this field.
Storage iron is increased but sideroblasts are typically normal or increased rather than reduced.
Precipitate lies on top of cells and in the background as irregular crystals, whereas hemosiderin is confined within macrophage cytoplasm.
